title: Arrival
objective: Find a bed. Find out who remembers [missing person].

text.default:
The barge comes in at nightfall, and the ferryman ties off without a word. For the last hour you have watched Crestfall grow out of a few lamps on the water into a town you know, and now that it is in front of you, you rather wish you had looked the other way.

You left eleven years ago and told yourself you were not coming back. You said it often enough that you very nearly believed it.

The docks smell of rot and cold water. A warehouse door hangs open on a broken hinge, and somewhere up in the town a dog is barking and getting no answer. You pick up your pack, step off onto the pier and stand there a little while, getting your bearings.
text.commander:
From the water you could see how much smaller the town has become. It has the look of a place that has been losing people slowly for years, and has stopped expecting them back.

You left because there was a war, and a war at least gave orders that made sense. You have come back because of a letter, from somebody whose name you do not say in company.
text.arcane:
You stayed awake the whole crossing, watching the water. The river changes as it nears Crestfall. Nothing shows on the surface, but underneath there is a pressure you feel in your teeth more than hear. You first noticed it two miles out, and you still could not tell anyone what it is.

It is stronger on land. Whatever is here, it is making no effort to hide.
text.ranger:
You look the docks over as you would a tree line. The dog to the north keeps barking at the same thing, so it is frightened or puzzled, probably both. The warehouse hinge has rusted open. Nobody has used that door in weeks.

You grew up knowing every yard of this place, and a good deal of it has moved.
text.cipher:
You watched the ferryman's back the whole way in. He has not said a word since you paid him two days ago. From the water you counted what the town shows a stranger: too few lights, and a Compact soldier on the gate at this hour, which is new.

Something has happened here, and very likely more than one thing.

choices.text: Go into town and find somewhere to sleep.

default.text: You walk up the pier towards the gate. The cobbles are just as uneven as they were, and the cold comes off the river exactly as it used to. It is you that has changed, you suppose, or the town. You cannot yet tell which.

choices.text: Stand on the pier and take stock of what has changed.

success.text:
You stand still and count, and you have found seven things wrong before you move. There is a Compact soldier on the gate, and no lights in the market. The river birds have gone quiet. The east side has its windows boarded, the shrine is no longer where it stood for forty years, and there is a smell of burning that is not woodsmoke. And the dog has still not stopped.

You do not write any of it down. You find you have no trouble remembering.

success_at_cost.text: You take in some of it: the Compact soldier, the dark market, the river with no birds on it. That is enough to tell you the town has changed in ways eleven years do not account for. But the crossing has tired you out, and after a while you give up counting and start walking.

failure.text: You stand on the pier and look at Crestfall, and that is all you manage. You are too tired from the crossing to make anything of it, and you know it. You start walking before you can talk yourself into standing there till morning.

text.default:
A man is coiling rope by the warehouse, or making a show of it. He has been watching you since you stepped off the barge. As you come nearer he straightens up, and you know him. It is Sen, from the docks, from the years before you went.

He is greyer than he was, and more weathered, in the way people get from staying somewhere hard rather than leaving it.

"Didn't think you'd come back," he says. "Nobody comes back."

He glances at the town behind him as if he is not sure it is still there.
text.commander: You knew him before he knew you. Sen used to load supplies for the garrison when you were posted here. He was a reliable man, and he noticed a great deal and said very little about it.
text.arcane:
You know the name from eleven years ago, and the face only just. He has changed more than eleven years ought to change a man.

"Especially not now," he adds, and looks as though he wishes he had not.
text.ranger:
He knew you were there before the barge was in. You saw him stiffen while you were still fifty yards out.

You hunted with his father once, before you left. Sen has his father's hands. When he talks he looks at the tree line to the east, and not at you.
text.cipher: You had a minute to study him while pretending not to. His shoulders are tight. He is afraid, and has been for some time, and your arrival has given him one more thing to be afraid of. He says very little, but he means a good deal by it.

choices.text: "I'm looking for someone. You might have seen them."

success.text:
He lets out a breath, and looks tired more than anything.

"I know who you mean," he says. "Everyone here does." He looks about the docks. "They came through about fourteen months ago, asking questions. Then they stopped asking and started going into the forest instead." He stops. "Nobody goes into the forest."

He gives you a name, Maret, the woman who runs the camp outside town. He says it quickly, as though he has been carrying it about and is glad to put it down.

success_at_cost.text: He nods. "Fourteen months back, near enough. Asking round town about the old ruins. Then they weren't asking any more." He leaves it there. "Find Maret," he says, and he won't say anything else.

failure.text: He becomes careful at once. "Can't say I remember anyone in particular," he says, which is not at all the same as saying he doesn't. "Lots of people pass through."

choices.text: "What happened to this place?"

success.text:
He looks at the town a while before he answers.

"It started with the animals," he says. "Two years ago. They moved wrong. Then it was the crops, and then people started going quiet. Not sad, just quiet. Like something had been turned down in them."

He looks at the river. "Some came back out of it. Some didn't."

success_at_cost.text: "Things change," he says. Then, lower: "The forest started coming closer. That's how it felt, anyway. Like the trees were paying more attention than they used to." He shakes his head. "Get yourself a room at the Tallow. And don't go east."

failure.text: "Same as everywhere," he says. That isn't true, and he knows you know it. He goes back to his rope.

choices.text: Nod and move past him into town.

default.text: You nod to him and walk on. You can feel him watching you for some way up the street. He has more to tell you, you think, and has decided you are not ready to hear it.

text.default:
The Tallow is quieter than you remember. On a cold night it used to be loud, with arguments about harvest weights and somebody playing a fiddle badly by the fire. Now three men sit at separate tables and say nothing to one another, and the fire is lower than it ought to be at this hour.

The innkeeper looks up as you come in. It is Aldous, and he knows you at once. You watch him decide what to make of it.

"Didn't think we'd see you back here," he says. He says it neither warmly nor coldly, rather as a man remarks on the weather.

You put your pack down by the door. The low beam you always had to duck is still there, and so is the loose board in front of the bar.
text.commander:
You have slept in worse places, you remind yourself. Aldous has the look of a man who has waited so long for bad news that any news now seems bad to him at first.

He does not ask why you have come back, or why now. You can see that he would like to.
text.arcane:
The room has a residue. It is not the curse, quite. People have been frightened in this one room for so long that the fear has got into the wood and the plaster.

Aldous means his greeting plainly enough, but it doesn't come out that way.
text.ranger:
The fire is low, so either wood is short or nobody can be bothered to see to it. The three men are regulars, by the way they sit, and they have simply given up sitting together.

Aldous's hands go still when he sees you. He looks at your pack, then at the door behind you, and then at you again.
text.cipher:
The three men are careful not to look at each other, as people do when they have agreed not to talk about something. Nobody is seeing to the fire.

You watch Aldous recognise you. He is pleased for a moment, and then wary, and then he is plainly doing a sum: what he owes you from before, against how much trouble you are likely to be now.

choices.text: "I'm looking for someone. Their name is [missing person]."

success.text:
He puts down the cloth he was wiping the bar with.

"I know that name," he says at last. "Came through about fourteen months ago, asking about the old ruins to the east. Stayed three weeks. Got friendly with the Rootless, the people in the camp outside town. Then one morning they'd gone, and nobody saw them go."

He pours something and puts it in front of you without being asked. "You family?"

success_at_cost.text:
He stops for a moment. Then he picks up his cloth and goes on wiping.

"That name means something," he says. "Can't say more tonight. You've only just got here. Get some sleep. Things look clearer in the morning."

He names a price for the room. It is too high, and he knows it is. He is not turning you away, you realise. He is making you wait.

failure.text:
His face shuts, politely but firmly.

"Can't say I know that name," he says. You notice he hasn't said he doesn't know it, only that he can't say.

He slides a key across the bar without looking at you.

choices.text: Order a drink and ask about the price of lamp oil.

default.text:
He tells you the price. Then he tells you what it was last year, and the year before, and who in town is buying it by the barrel and what for. By the time he has done he is leaning on the bar and has quite forgotten to be careful.

"You'll be wanting a room," he says, and this time he doesn't make it a question.

choices.text: Say nothing. Take a seat by the fire and watch.

success.text:
You sit by the fire and watch.

The three men are regulars; you can tell by the way they sit, each in a chair he has worn to his own shape. They have simply stopped talking to each other.

The man nearest the fire has not moved since you sat down. His drink has not been touched. His eyes are open and fixed on something that is not in the room.

Aldous watches him too, when he thinks nobody is looking. He is worried, you can see, and he has also made up his mind that there is nothing to be done.

success_at_cost.text: You sit, and the room tells you a little. The man by the fire is wrong. He is too still and his eyes are fixed on nothing. Aldous keeps looking at him, but from where you are you cannot make out what he thinks about it.

failure.text: You sit. The fire is low and the three men drink in silence while Aldous wipes the bar. You are too tired to make anything of it tonight, so you go up to the bar and pay for a room.

choices.text: "A room for the night. Whatever you have."

default.text: "Four coins," Aldous says. It is too much, and he says it anyway. You pay. He slides the key across the bar and goes back to what he was doing, and you go upstairs.

text.default:
You sit at the bar and Aldous talks. He weighs every word, but he does talk.

Fourteen months ago [missing person] came to town and spent a week asking questions nobody wanted to answer, about the ruins to the east and the old city under the forest. Then they found the Rootless camp, where the people the town turned out are living, and spent the next two weeks there.

"The woman at the camp," Aldous says. "Maret. She knew them better than I did, by the end. She might tell you something, or she might not." He fills his own glass for the first time tonight. "Mostly she doesn't."

He looks at you. "I hope you find what you're after. And I hope it's still what you think it is when you do."
text.commander:
Aldous tells you what he knows because you asked him properly, straight out and without leaning on him. You have had to get information out of people before.

Fourteen months ago, he says, and they held themselves like a soldier; he noticed that. They asked the right questions, stayed three weeks, and were gone one morning without a word.

"Maret would know more," he says. "She's careful who she talks to, but she's not hard."
text.arcane:
Aldous tells you what he knows, and it turns out to be more than he thought. You have often noticed this about people. They start with what they are sure of and end up somewhere they did not expect.

Fourteen months ago, questions about the ruins, three weeks of talking to Maret at the camp, and then gone. They did not run away, he thinks. They had made up their minds about something.

"Whatever they were after," Aldous says slowly, "I think they'd found the start of it."
text.ranger:
Aldous talks and you listen as you would listen to a hillside, for which way things are moving.

Fourteen months ago [missing person] arrived and asked about the ruins. They spent three weeks at the Rootless camp, and then they went east and told nobody.

"Maret," Aldous says. "At the camp. She's the one to find." And then, flatly: "Don't go into the forest on your own."
text.cipher:
Aldous tells you what he knows, and you pay as much attention to what he leaves out.

He does not say whether he tried to stop them, and he makes the Rootless camp sound rather more harmless than you suspect it is. He is not lying, you think. There are simply things he has decided you ought to find out for yourself.

choices.text: "Tell me about Maret."

success.text:
He thinks about it. "She came to Crestfall about three years ago with six people and a cart. Said they were passing through. They never left, and the camp grew." He stops. "She's good at finding the people the town doesn't know what to do with. The sick ones, the ones whose families won't speak to them any more. She takes them in."

After a while he goes on. "People say things about her. That she's made some sort of arrangement with whatever's in the forest. I don't know if it's true. I know her people are alive when others aren't."

success_at_cost.text: "She runs the camp outside town," he says. "Three years she's been there. Keeps herself to herself, mostly." He stops. There is more, you can see, but he has already said more tonight than he meant to.

failure.text: "She can speak for herself," Aldous says. It is no answer at all, and you let it go.

choices.text: "What's in the forest? What's causing all this?"

success.text:
He pours himself another drink, and a large one.

"Nobody knows. Or nobody agrees. The Covenant says it's a punishment. The Compact says it's a resource to be managed. The Rootless say it was always there, and something cracked and let it out." He drinks. "I've lived here forty years. The forest was never friendly, but it was quiet. It kept to itself." He lowers his voice. "Two years ago it stopped keeping to itself."

success_at_cost.text: He shakes his head. "If I knew that I'd have left, or fixed it." He wipes the bar again. "Get some sleep. Questions are easier when you're not falling over."

failure.text: "That's a question for people who know more than I do," he says. "In this town that's either the Covenant or nobody."

choices.text: Thank him and go to your room.

default.text: "Three coins," he says. That is under the posted rate. You take the key and go upstairs.

text.default:
You take the room for four coins. It is too much, and you both know it, and neither of you mentions it.

Aldous hands over the key briskly, like a man who has made up his mind. He has decided that tonight he will say nothing about [missing person], and he is sticking to it.

You carry your pack upstairs. The landing smells of old wood and the heat is uneven. The room has a bed, a lamp, and a window on the street, and it will do.

You sit on the bed and listen to the inn: the three men downstairs, the fire settling, Aldous moving about behind the bar. Outside there is the wind, and under the wind something you cannot put a name to, which may be nothing at all.
text.commander:
You pay the four coins without remark. Aldous gives you the key and does not quite look at you, which tells you something.

The room will do. The window looks east. In the morning you will try him again, with more time and a clearer head. Some ground is taken by waiting rather than by force.
text.arcane:
The old fear is strongest on the upper landing. It has had years to settle into the place. Nothing in particular happened here, you think. People have simply been frightened for a long time.

You sit at the window and write up your notes. The pressure you felt on the river is here too, very faint, like a word in a language you nearly speak.
text.ranger:
You pay. The room will do, and better than that, it is on the corner, with a window on each street. It is an old habit.

You do not go to sleep at once. You sit in the dark and listen to Crestfall at night. There are fewer animals than there should be, and the ones that are left are moving about at the wrong hours.
text.cipher:
You pay the four coins and are careful not to make a point of it. Aldous hands you the key, and you both behave as though the last five minutes had gone quite differently.

You sit in the dark and go over what you have learned in your first two hours. Aldous knows something, and he has decided to make you earn it. That means it can be earned, which is something.

choices.text: Sleep. Start fresh in the morning.

default.text: You sleep badly and wake before dawn, wide awake and no more rested. You dress and go downstairs.

choices.text: Go back downstairs and try again while the inn is still open.

success.text:
He is surprised to see you back so soon, and you take advantage of it. You ask him again, more gently, and this time he answers.

"Fourteen months," he says. "Maret at the camp would know more than me." He seems glad to have it said.

success_at_cost.text: He looks up when you come back down. He tells you about the Rootless camp, and about Maret. He does not tell you how he knows she knew [missing person].

failure.text: He has made up his mind, and you cannot change it tonight. He gives you a drink on the house and nothing else, and you go back upstairs.

text.default:
You have the key. Aldous has found something behind the bar that needs all his attention, and the three men at their tables are very carefully not listening.

You go upstairs.

The room cost four coins, and the window looks out on a street where nothing moves. You sit on the bed. Aldous knows [missing person]'s name, you are sure of it, and tonight he is keeping it to himself.

You have been back in Crestfall less than an hour and you have already made a mistake. You do not intend to make it twice.
text.commander: You have had men shut up under questioning before, and you know what it looks like. Aldous isn't hostile. He is frightened of something, and you reminded him of it. That can be put right. Tomorrow you will go about it differently.
text.arcane: You sit by the window and write it down. The innkeeper knows the name. He showed it before he could stop himself, and then he decided it was safer to say nothing. What he is afraid of is what you need to know, and you do not know it yet.
text.ranger:
On your way to bed you take stock of the room. Aldous looks guilty. The other two men were not surprised. Whatever is wrong with the still man by the fire has nothing to do with your question.

You asked badly. In the morning you will come at it another way, through the Rootless camp, probably.
text.cipher:
A beginner's mistake, and the mistake was letting him see how much it mattered to you. People who know something can tell when you need it, and it makes them careful.

Aldous isn't your enemy. He is a frightened man in a frightened town, and you asked him the wrong way at the wrong time. It can be put right tomorrow.

choices.text: Sleep, and try a different approach tomorrow.

default.text: You sleep anyway. You learned how to a long time ago.

choices.text: Sit by the fire a while before you go up.

default.text: You take the chair nearest the fire. The man on the other side of it doesn't look up.

text.default:
You go over to the man by the fire. You do not creep up on him, but you do not make a noise about it either, so that he can ignore you if he likes.

He does not ignore you. His eyes follow you as you come near, so he knows you are there, and whatever this is, it is not sleep.

He is somewhere in his forties, with a farmer's hands. His ale has gone flat and cold. He has been sitting there a very long while.

"Evening," you say.

He opens his mouth and shuts it again. "Evening," he says at last. His voice is perfectly ordinary, and somehow that is worse.
text.commander:
You go about it directly. You pull a chair round and sit down opposite him.

It takes him a while to find you. When he speaks his voice is quite ordinary, as flat as if he were talking about the price of feed.

"I know what you're looking at," he says. "My wife looks at me the same way."

He looks at his hands. "I can feel it, mostly. Like sitting in cold water. After a while you stop noticing the cold."
text.arcane:
You sit down opposite him, and the residue on him is stronger than anything else in the inn. It is the curse, but not pressing on him from outside. He has breathed it in for months, and it has become part of him.

He knows you are there. His eyes come round to you slowly, as though they were moving through water.

"You can see it, can't you," he says. "I could tell, the way you looked at me when you came in." Then, after a while: "I don't know how to stop it. I've tried."
text.ranger:
You crouch down beside him instead of sitting, as you would with a hurt animal, so as to seem smaller.

He looks at you, and there is more of him there than you expected.

"It's worse in the evenings," he says slowly. "I lose the thread of things. I'm here, and then I'm somewhere else, without moving. Just somewhere else in my head." His hands close round the cold glass. "Three months now."
text.cipher:
You sit down opposite him with a drink you have no intention of finishing, and wait for him to notice you.

He does, eventually.

"You're new," he says. His voice is quite normal, which is the unsettling part.

"Just arrived," you say.

"Don't go east," he says at once. Then: "Sorry. I say that to everyone now. My wife says it's the only thing I talk about." He considers this. "She's not wrong."

choices.text: Ask him what it feels like from inside.

success.text:
He tells you, slowly. He has been looking for the words for some time, and he seems glad to have someone to say them to.

It started as tiredness, he says, and then he began to feel a long way off, as if he were watching his own life through a window. First he stopped wanting things, then he stopped caring about them, and then he stopped noticing them. He can still think, but the thoughts feel borrowed, like another man's coat.

"I don't want to go any further in," he says. "But I don't know how to get back, either." He looks at the fire. "Some of them go further in and they look peaceful. I think about that, sometimes."

success_at_cost.text:
He tries. He talks about being tired, and far off, and about things that used to matter not mattering. He stops before he has finished, and you cannot tell whether he has lost the thread or simply decided not to go on.

"You should get your room," he says at last. "Aldous keeps good rooms."

failure.text: He tries to answer and cannot find the words. He shakes his head very slightly, as if even that costs him something, and turns back to the fire.

choices.text: Leave him to it. Go to the bar instead.

default.text: You get up and go to the bar. Aldous watches you come. "He's been like that two months," he says, though you didn't ask. "His name's Wren. He's a good man." He stops. "Was. Is." He doesn't seem to know which.

default: The room is small and will do. There is a bed, a window, and a lamp with oil for two more hours if you are careful. The street below is empty.
You sit on the bed and let the day settle.

default.text: Two streets over is the east field fence. You and [missing person] ran the length of it every summer, one foot on the top rail, and whoever fell off first paid for the cider.
The lamp is the same kind they used to read by, in the room above the chandler's. They read with their knees drawn up and their lips moving. You used to pretend to be asleep so you could watch.
From this window you can almost see the mill lane. [missing person] used to sit on the wall at the end of it and wait for you to come home, two years younger and pretending not to wait.

The last time you were in this inn, [missing person] bought you a drink for finishing your first real piece of work. They did not say well done. They pushed the cup across the table and watched you drink it.

[missing person] used to bring you here on market days when you were small, and sit you on the bar while they argued about the price of lamp oil. You remember the smell of the wood, and their hand flat on your back.

You stood under this window once with [missing person], waiting out the rain. Neither of you said anything the whole time. You have thought about that silence more than most things anyone has said to you.

default: So you are back in Crestfall, and the town has gone wrong in ways that eleven years cannot explain. The person you came for was here fourteen months ago and is here no longer. A woman called Maret may know where they went, and everything you have heard points east, to the forest.

Outside, the wind goes through a town that has stopped making most of its noises. You try to remember how Crestfall sounded at this hour, and find that you can, mostly, which makes the quiet harder to bear.

choices.text: Go on.

default: You take the letter out again. There is no need; you know it by heart.

default.text:
> [player],
> I am in Crestfall. The east field fence is still standing. Nobody walks it.
> There is something under the forest and I think I can find it.
> I am not asking you to come.
> [missing person]

> [player],
> I am in Crestfall. I did not know whether to write. I am writing.
> There is something under the forest and I think I can find it.
> I am not asking you to come.
> [missing person]

> [player],
> I am in Crestfall. The house has new shutters. I let it go in the end.
> There is something under the forest and I think I can find it.
> I am not asking you to come.
> [missing person]

> [player],
> I am in Crestfall. You will want to know I was right about the forest.
> There is something under the forest and I think I can find it.
> I am not asking you to come.
> [missing person]

> [player],
> I am in Crestfall. I have not stopped being angry. I wanted you to know where I am anyway.
> There is something under the forest and I think I can find it.
> I am not asking you to come.
> [missing person]

> [player],
> I am in Crestfall. I have started this letter eleven times.
> There is something under the forest and I think I can find it.
> I am not asking you to come.
> [missing person]

default: You put out the lamp, and after a while you sleep.
text.commander:
You go over the position as you would any other. You know the name, the direction they went, and how long ago. You do not know much else. You have yourself, what you carried, and the fact that you are exactly what you look like, which people tend to trust.

You sleep as soldiers learn to, lightly and at once.
text.arcane:
You write by lamplight until you have to save the oil.

The pressure under Crestfall is steady, like a string that has been plucked and has not yet stopped sounding. You have felt something of the kind near old workings before, but those were much smaller.

You write: whatever is here has been here a very long time. The curse did not make it. The curse is what happens when something holds it badly.
text.ranger:
You leave the lamp unlit. You sit in the dark by the window until your eyes have adjusted, and watch the street for an hour. Nothing moves that shouldn't.

But there are no animals. In any town, at any hour, there ought to be something about, a cat or a dog going by. There is nothing at all.

You sleep lightly, with one ear on the window.
text.cipher:
You spend an hour sorting out what you were told from what you only guessed: Maret, the camp, the forest, fourteen months.

Aldous has kept something back, and so has Sen at the docks. That gives you plenty to work on in the morning.

choices.text: Wake early and explore the town before most people are up.

default.text: You wake before dawn. Aldous is already behind the bar with a cup of something he doesn't offer to share. You take some bread from the board by the door and go out into Crestfall.

choices.text: You can't sleep. Go back down and sit with the man by the fire.

default.text: The common room is nearly empty. The man is still in the chair by the fire, just where he was.

default: You don't remember how it ended.

default.text:
You wake under canvas, with the smell of the camp fire and somebody's coat over you. It is morning, and you have lost a day.

Maret is sitting on an upturned crate by the tent flap. "Branch carried you," she says. "Do not thank him. He will not know what to do with it."

You wake on a pallet at the back of the shrine, under the grey banner. It is morning, and a day has gone.

Edric is lighting the candles one at a time. "You were found on the steps," he says, without turning round.

You wake by the fire in the outskirts. The light is the same grey as always, but [missing person] tells you a day has gone.

"You stopped," they say. "In the middle of a sentence. I talked to you until you came back."

You wake in a room at the Tallow with your boots still on. The light says it is morning, and the wrong morning, too, for a day has gone. Somebody has left water by the bed and a heel of bread on a plate.

Aldous is in the doorway. "Two of them brought you in," he says. "I didn't ask where from."

default: You sit up. Your hands are steady enough.

choices.text: Get up.

default.text: You get dressed and go back out.
